name: Differential Privacy
description: Differentially private mechanisms, analytics, and deployments, including local DP.
narrative:
Differential privacy at USENIX Security began less as a quest to invent new mechanisms and more as a reckoning with how the theory holds up in practice. The earliest listed work, "Evaluating Differentially Private Machine Learning in Practice" (2019), confronted the gap between DP's strong formal guarantees and what actually happens when you train models under realistic privacy budgets, showing that the choice of epsilon and accounting method dramatically shapes the privacy-utility trade-off. Alongside it, "When the Signal is in the Noise: Exploiting Diffix's Sticky Noise" (2019) attacked a deployed anonymization system, a reminder that ad-hoc "noise" schemes that lack DP's rigor can be broken. Early deployments also began appearing, such as "Differentially-Private Control-Flow Node Coverage for Software Usage Analysis" (2020), which applied DP to a concrete telemetry-collection problem.

The next phase broadened DP from a single-model property to a building block for distributed and richer data settings. Federated learning became a major proving ground: "PrivateFL: Accurate, Differentially Private Federated Learning via Personalized Data Transformation" (2023) tackled the accuracy cost of DP in federated training, while work expanded DP to structured data with "PrivGraph: Differentially Private Graph Data Publication by Exploiting Community Information" (2023). At the same time, the community turned to the human and usability side of DP, asking whether anyone could actually interpret its central knob in "What Are the Chances? Explaining the Epsilon Parameter in Differential Privacy" (2023).

By 2024 the area matured into specialized mechanisms and a serious focus on local DP. Generative modeling met DP in "dp-promise: Differentially Private Diffusion Probabilistic Models for Image Synthesis" (2024), and training techniques were refined in "DPAdapter: Improving Differentially Private Deep Learning through Noise Tolerance Pre-training" (2024) and "Closed-Form Bounds for DP-SGD against Record-level Inference" (2024). Local DP, where noise is added at the source, grew into a subfield of its own with "Relation Mining Under Local Differential Privacy" (2024) pushing LDP beyond simple statistics.

Most recently the frontier has shifted toward auditing and verification: rather than trusting that a mechanism satisfies its claimed guarantee, researchers now empirically test it. "Privacy Audit as Bits Transmission: (Im)possibilities for Audit by One Run" (2025) and "General-Purpose f-DP Estimation and Auditing in a Black-Box Setting" (2025) treat DP guarantees as something to be measured and falsified, while local DP continues to be refined for utility in "Addressing Sensitivity Distinction in Local Differential Privacy: A General Utility-Optimized Framework" (2025). The arc runs from questioning whether DP works in practice, to deploying it across federated and graph data, to building tools that hold its guarantees accountable.
